works/book-of-1-enoch/summary: Jewish apocalyptic text expanding Genesis 6:1-4: angelic Watchers led by Shemihazah and Asael descend, take human wives, teach forbidden arts and beget giants, bringing violence until judgement.
works/book-of-1-enoch/significance: Canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church and quoted in Jude 14-15; foundational for Second Temple and early Christian demonology.
works/athanasius-life-of-antony/summary: Athanasius’ biography of the desert father Antony, including his long discourse on the deceits of demons and how to discern and resist them.
works/athanasius-life-of-antony/signific: Shaped monastic demonology and the ideal of the monk as spiritual warrior.
works/pseudo-dionysius-celestial-hierarc: Arranges the nine angelic orders in three triads, each mediating divine illumination to the one below.
The classic Christian angelology, normative in medieval East and West.
works/gregory-homilies-gospels/summary: Homilies preached in Rome; Homily 34 on the lost sheep and coin discusses the nine orders of angels.
works/gregory-homilies-gospels/significa: Transmitted an angelic hierarchy to the medieval West.
works/summis-desiderantes/summary: Bull of Innocent VIII authorising Kramer and Sprenger to prosecute witchcraft in Germany.
works/summis-desiderantes/significance: Lent papal authority to the inquisitors; printed with the Malleus.
works/malleus-maleficarum/summary: Manual arguing that witchcraft is real, a pact with the devil involving chiefly women, and a crime to be prosecuted by secular courts using torture.
works/malleus-maleficarum/significance: Widely reprinted; a significant though not singular influence on early modern witch-hunting.
works/luther-mighty-fortress/title: A Mighty Fortress Is Our God (Ein feste Burg)
works/luther-mighty-fortress/summary: Luther’s hymn on Psalm 46 portraying the Christian’s battle with the devil, overcome by Christ.
works/luther-mighty-fortress/significanc: The “battle hymn of the Reformation”, sung across denominations.
works/rituale-romanum-exorcism/title: Rituale Romanum, Title XII: On Exorcising the Possessed
works/rituale-romanum-exorcism/summary: The rite of solemn exorcism issued under Paul V, with criteria for discerning possession and cautions against superstition.
works/spee-cautio-criminalis/summary: Anonymous critique of witch-trial procedure, especially torture, by a confessor of condemned witches.
works/spee-cautio-criminalis/significanc: One of the most influential arguments that hastened the decline of witch trials in Germany.
works/bekker-world-bewitched/summary: Argues from Scripture and Cartesian philosophy that spirits cannot act on bodies and that belief in witchcraft is unfounded.
works/bekker-world-bewitched/significanc: Major early Enlightenment attack on demonology from within the Reformed church.
works/mather-cases-of-conscience/title: Cases of Conscience concerning Evil Spirits Personating Men
works/mather-cases-of-conscience/summary: Argues that spectral evidence (testimony that the accused’s spectre afflicted someone) is unreliable because the devil can impersonate the innocent.
works/mather-cases-of-conscience/signifi: Contributed to ending the Salem trials.
works/bultmann-nt-mythology/summary: Argues that the New Testament’s three-storey universe of spirits and demons is mythological and must be interpreted existentially for modern people.
works/lewis-screwtape-letters/summary: Satirical letters from a senior devil to his nephew on tempting a human “patient”.
works/lewis-screwtape-letters/significan: Popular modern Christian treatment of demonic temptation.
works/wink-naming-the-powers/summary: First volume of the Powers trilogy, a word study and theology of New Testament power language.
works/wink-naming-the-powers/significanc: Reframed the powers as spiritual-institutional realities.
works/de-exorcismis-1999/summary: The revised Catholic Rite of Exorcism, promulgated in January 1999, requiring careful discernment including medical and psychiatric assessment.
works/de-exorcismis-1999/significance: Replaced the 1614 rite; an English translation was approved in 2017.
works/abelard-commentary-romans/title: Commentary on the Epistle to the Romans
works/abelard-commentary-romans/summary: Abelard’s commentary, whose excursus on Romans 3:19-26 asks to whom a ransom could be paid and answers that Christ’s passion reveals and kindles love in us.
works/abelard-commentary-romans/signific: Locus classicus of the "moral influence" (exemplarist) view; attacked by Bernard of Clairvaux.
works/anselm-cur-deus-homo/title: Why God Became Man (Cur Deus Homo)
works/anselm-cur-deus-homo/summary: A dialogue with the monk Boso arguing "by necessary reasons" that only a God-man could render the satisfaction owed to God’s honour by sinful humanity.
works/anselm-cur-deus-homo/significance: Origin of the satisfaction theory; it displaced the idea of rights of the devil and set the agenda for Western atonement theology.
works/aulen-christus-victor-work/title: Christus Victor: An Historical Study of the Three Main Types of the Idea of the Atonement
works/aulen-christus-victor-work/summary: Aulén's Uppsala lectures (1930; English 1931) arguing that the 'classic' patristic and Lutheran idea of the atonement is God's victory in Christ over sin, death and the devil, distinct from the Latin (satisfaction) and subjective (moral influence) types.
works/aulen-christus-victor-work/signifi: Revived the dramatic "victory" model across denominations.
works/campbell-nature-of-atonement/summa: Campbell's mature work after his deposition (1831): Christ's atoning work is a perfect confession of and repentance for humanity's sin, a 'perfect Amen' to God's judgement, revealing the Father's love; atonement is filial and relational rather than legal.
works/campbell-nature-of-atonement/signi: Seminal for the Torrances and for relational, union-centred accounts of the atonement.
works/gregory-nyssa-catechetical-oration: A manual for catechists explaining the Trinity, incarnation, redemption and sacraments; chapters 22-26 present the ransom as a just deception of the devil (the "fish-hook" image).
Classic statement of the patristic ransom motif.
works/grotius-defensio/title: Defence of the Catholic Faith concerning the Satisfaction of Christ against Faustus Socinus (Defensio fidei catholicae de satisfactione Christi)
works/grotius-defensio/summary: Against Socinus, Grotius defends the necessity of Christ’s death by casting God as Rector (governor) who relaxes the law for the elect while upholding moral order by a public example of punishment.
works/grotius-defensio/significance: Origin of the "governmental" theory; influential in New England theology and Methodism.
works/nazianzen-letter-to-cledonius/titl: Letter 101 to Cledonius (First Letter against Apollinarius)
works/nazianzen-letter-to-cledonius/summ: Letter against Apollinarius insisting that Christ assumed a complete human nature, including a rational mind, because "that which He has not assumed He has not healed".
works/nazianzen-letter-to-cledonius/sign: Classic statement of the soteriological principle behind Chalcedonian Christology and participatory atonement.
works/owen-death-of-death/title: The Death of Death in the Death of Christ
works/owen-death-of-death/summary: Owen's defence of definite (particular) redemption against universal redemption, arguing that Christ's death actually secures the salvation of those for whom it was intended.
works/owen-death-of-death/significance: The classic Reformed argument for limited atonement and for penal substitution understood as effective.
works/campbell-christian-system/summary: Campbell’s summary of Restorationist teaching, including immersion of penitent believers "for the remission of sins" (Acts 2:38) as the divinely appointed moment of forgiveness.
works/campbell-christian-system/signific: Defined the Stone-Campbell understanding of baptism.
works/cyril-mystagogical-catecheses/summ: Five post-baptismal lectures given in Easter week in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre explaining baptism, chrismation and the Eucharist to the newly baptized (authorship sometimes assigned to Cyril’s successor John).
works/cyril-mystagogical-catecheses/sign: A vivid witness to fourth-century baptismal rites: renunciation facing west, threefold immersion, anointing.
works/hubmaier-christian-baptism/title: On the Christian Baptism of Believers (Von der christlichen Taufe der Gläubigen)
works/hubmaier-christian-baptism/summary: Hubmaier’s systematic defence of believers’ baptism against Zwingli: the order of Christ’s command is preaching, faith, then baptism as a public pledge.
works/hubmaier-christian-baptism/signifi: The most learned early Anabaptist argument for believers’ baptism.
works/tertullian-on-baptism/summary: The oldest surviving Christian treatise on baptism, written against a Cainite teacher who denied its necessity; it defends water baptism and counsels delaying baptism for little children and the unmarried.
works/tertullian-on-baptism/significance: Earliest evidence both for infant baptism being practised and for a dissenting counsel to delay it.
works/ignatius-letter-to-the-ephesians/s: Written on the way to martyrdom in Rome, urging unity with the bishop and confessing Christ as both flesh and spirit, God in man.
One of the earliest post-New Testament statements of Christ's deity and humanity.
works/ignatius-letter-to-the-trallians/s: Warns against docetists who say Christ only seemed to suffer and insists on his true birth, suffering, death and resurrection.
works/ignatius-letter-to-the-smyrnaeans/: Against docetists: Christ truly suffered and rose in the flesh; the Eucharist is his flesh; ‘wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic Church’.
Earliest use of ‘catholic Church’ and an early witness to Eucharistic realism.
works/gregory-letter-101-cledonius/title: Letter 101, to Cledonius (First Letter against Apollinaris)
works/gregory-letter-101-cledonius/summa: Gregory's refutation of Apollinarianism, insisting that Christ assumed a complete human nature including a rational soul.
works/gregory-letter-101-cledonius/signi: Source of the principle ‘the unassumed is the unhealed’; read at Chalcedon.
works/cyril-third-letter-to-nestorius/ti: Third Letter to Nestorius, with the Twelve Anathemas
works/cyril-third-letter-to-nestorius/su: Cyril's synodical letter demanding that Nestorius confess the hypostatic union and Theotokos, ending in twelve anathemas.
works/cyril-third-letter-to-nestorius/si: Read at Ephesus (431); the anathemas remained controversial with Antiochenes but were later received at Constantinople II (553).
works/cyril-letters-to-succensus/summary: Two letters explaining, after the Formula of Reunion, how ‘one incarnate nature of God the Word’ is compatible with the integrity of Christ's humanity.
works/tome-of-leo/summary: Pope Leo I's dogmatic letter to Patriarch Flavian against Eutyches: one person, two natures, each acting in communion with the other.
works/tome-of-leo/significance: Acclaimed at Chalcedon (‘Peter has spoken through Leo’); rejected by Miaphysites as Nestorian.
works/chalcedonian-definition/title: Definition of Faith of the Council of Chalcedon
works/chalcedonian-definition/summary: Confesses one and the same Christ ‘in two natures, without confusion, without change, without division, without separation’, the properties of each preserved in one person and hypostasis; Mary called Theotokos.
works/chalcedonian-definition/significan: The standard of Christological orthodoxy for Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and most Protestant churches; the cause of the Oriental Orthodox separation.
works/maximus-disputation-with-pyrrhus/s: Record of Maximus' public debate at Carthage with the deposed patriarch Pyrrhus, in which Maximus argues that will belongs to nature, so Christ has two wills.
The central text of dyothelite Christology.
works/schleiermacher-christian-faith/sum: A dogmatics grounded in the feeling of absolute dependence; Christ is the Redeemer through the perfect potency of his God-consciousness. Second edition 1830–31.
works/schleiermacher-christian-faith/sig: The founding work of liberal Protestant theology.
works/clement-1-clement/title: First Epistle of Clement to the Corinthians
works/clement-1-clement/summary: Letter from the church of Rome to the church of Corinth urging the restoration of deposed presbyters.
works/clement-1-clement/significance: Earliest non-canonical Christian letter; chapters 42–44 give an early theory of apostolic appointment and succession of church leaders.
works/ignatius-to-the-smyrnaeans/summary: One of seven letters written by Ignatius of Antioch on his way to martyrdom in Rome.
works/ignatius-to-the-smyrnaeans/signifi: Contains the first use of "the Catholic Church" and strong statements on the bishop and on the Eucharist as Christ’s flesh.
works/justin-first-apology/summary: Defence of Christianity addressed to Emperor Antoninus Pius.
works/justin-first-apology/significance: Chapters 61–67 give the earliest detailed description of Christian baptism and Sunday Eucharist.
works/cyprian-unity-of-the-church/title: On the Unity of the Catholic Church (De Unitate)
works/cyprian-unity-of-the-church/summar: Cyprian’s tract against the Novatianist schism, insisting on the unity of the episcopate.
works/cyprian-unity-of-the-church/signif: Classic statement that there is no salvation outside the Church; its chapter 4 exists in two versions (one more papal), debated since the Reformation.
